candidates.why: info->sections is calloc'd at 2872 with info->num_sections elements (num_sections computed at 2867-2869 from ssize/max_decomp_size). section_info_rebuild writes info->sections[ssi] at 1736 where ssi counts every header.section entry with sec->type==type (loop 1731-1741), with no bound check against info->num_sections. If the real section count for that type exceeds num_sections, this writes past the heap buffer, corrupting adjacent chunks that are later used/freed.

dwg->header.section_info is realloc'd at 2843-2845. find_section_info_type (1712) returns a pointer into that array, and section_info_rebuild dereferences info->sections at 1736. If section_info is reallocated (moving the array) between obtaining info and the write, info dangles. In current call sites (2883, 2921) the realloc happens before the call, so this is a latent hazard rather than a confirmed bug.

header.section is realloc'd at 2878 (and 2919), invalidating all Dwg_Section* stored in info->sections[]. section_info_rebuild is only invoked when dwg->header.section != oldsecs (2881-2883). If realloc returns the same address but the array was logically resized, or if rebuild is skipped for some info entries (e.g. type > lasttype), stale pointers into the old buffer remain and are later dereferenced at 3077 (info->sections[k]).
